scope: First three tutorial levels; watercolor background and prop appearance studies.

assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create ORIGINAL watercolor storybook puzzle-platform game concept art for 食光兽. A small wandering lamplighter explores an abandoned botanical garden, feeding sunlight to tiny exposed areas of a single immobile enormous creature. The camera is actual SIDE-ON 2D gameplay framing, with three lightly layered depth planes to suggest a 3D space. NO isometric, NO axonometric map, NO overhead map, NO floating diorama, NO full creature, no full face. Only a local cropped soft living surface fits at the edge of the scene.
ART DIRECTION: unmistakably HAND-PAINTED TRANSLUCENT WATERCOLOR on visible cold-pressed ivory paper. Pigment blooms, granulation, soft wet edges, sparse delicate brown ink contours, large intentional paper-white spaces, flat illustrated shapes and decorative botanical rhythm. An artful fairy-tale picture-book, contemplative, tender and slightly mysterious. Palette pale apricot sunlight, soft sage/teal foliage, dusty lilac shadows, terracotta and ivory. Avoid photorealism, rendered game-engine lighting, polished digital painting, gritty gray medieval-city clutter, shiny metallic realism. The structural clarity and framing of an illustrated puzzle book, but original content.
READABILITY: darker simple foreground silhouettes, clear midground walkable platform edges, quieter distant shapes. One tiny dark-coated lamplighter with a small tool satchel per camera view, character height about 1/14 of image height. Platforms, steps, walls, door openings and all interactive props must be unmistakable, no confusing decorative fake platforms. The giant's exposed surface is SOFT warm ivory/peach skin with fine velvet hairs and a few translucent almond-shaped scales, faint breath folds, never cracked masonry. Its body extends beyond the frame so only the specified tiny portion is visible. The feeding patch is organic pearly amber, not a button, lamp, metal apparatus or glowing wall gemstone.
MIRROR INVARIANT: a brass oval mirror mounted on a VERTICAL spindle, on a fixed low gray stone foot, mirror plane remains UPRIGHT. It rotates LEFT/RIGHT in YAW around vertical axis, like a door on a vertical hinge. NO upward/downward tilting or floor-facing mirror. Its small operating knob is within the character's reach, and the upper mirror center is 1.8 character-heights above walkable ground. Sunlight in playable space travels at that fixed height in the horizontal world plane. A faint horizontal incoming beam may be shown, but do NOT draw a solved outgoing beam through walls. Final optical solution belongs in the separate technical drawing.
TEXT: only the specified concise Chinese heading/camera captions in a paper-white margin. No game HUD, no dimension numbers, no path arrows, no paragraphs, no overlaid maps. These are background design illustrations, not finished playable screenshots.
Output a single wide 16:9 background, large landscape format. Title in slim top paper margin: '01 借一束光｜门槛苔地'.
COMPOSITION anchored to the actual level: width around 20 character-heights, playable ground low in frame. LEFT edge: cropped gigantic wrought-iron garden gate, only a few bars and a pillar; morning horizontal light enters between bars at 1.8H, no rooftops in distance. Entry at lower-left. At x25% put a shallow harmless rain groove about 1.3H wide and 0.4H deep, followed by one mossy low stone step only 0.5H high; keep a walkable shallow bottom and low recovery slope. At x40% on the flat midground ledge stands the SINGLE small upright yaw-mirror, its stone base embedded and round pivot clear. Player stands beside it. Small flat clearing gives comfortable adjustment space.
RIGHT x78–90%: a VERY SMALL cropped tail-tip surface emerges from under the garden wall and moss at ground level, continues out of right edge. Fine peach fur, thin soft skin fold, one faint pearly feeding scale at same world height as mirror. It should initially resemble something hidden and alive rather than a whole tail. At far right x96% is an EXISTING low arch/crack leading toward the next overturned pot, gently obscured by one curled pale-green leaf; the leaf can unfold after feeding. The next pot appears only as a cropped terracotta rim at extreme right.
Keep at least upper third of sheet airy and pale, with sparse ivy and apricot mist. Include a small folded cloth and old twig near entry for the lamplighter's overnight shelter story. No new mechanics, no additional mirrors, no prism, no large chasm, no full beast. The only manipulative puzzle prop is the ONE yaw mirror. Initial light strikes its surface with a small glint; target remains dim, no complete solution path drawn.

Shared physical anchors in both views: one upside-down terracotta pot spanning right 60% of scene; a painted ivory crescent on rim; a thin old copper wire following a diagonal crack; one pale violet leaf beside its real REAR-SIDE break. Exactly ONE upright brass yaw mirror on a fixed stone foot outside the pot, near left quarter of main scene. A delicate twig-ring viewing point sits beside it on a safe broad floor (two small leaves on the ring indicate two views). No prism or interactive dew.
TOP A: flat SIDE ELEVATION from the garden-front. Entry low-left, mirror on flat ledge around x23%. The pot's front clay wall seems to block all light; a faint sunlit spot on clay makes the obstruction legible. Do not make the front clay wall transparent. Little mushrooms and one 0.4H-high porcelain shard step lead to an accessible side path around the pot, never a dangerous jump. The rear-side gap is hidden behind the pot curvature in this view. The little hero stands at the viewing ring looking toward the pot. The creature is only barely suggested by a few fine hairs under the far rim, no whole animal.
BOTTOM B: camera has moved 90 degrees around the pot, still rendered as a usable flat SIDE VIEW, revealing a REAL large broken side opening and, deeper inside, the NARROW actual passage through which the exterior mirror can send light. Keep the crescent mark, copper wire and violet leaf recognizable on the same clay rim. View into the pot through its actual break (not magic X-ray). Roots make a delicate curtain but leave a clear narrow unobstructed light corridor. A small exposed soft tail-belly patch presses gently against inner right wall, its organic feeding scale at 1.8H. The one external upright mirror is visible through the near opening, still in the same physical spot relative to pot. At inner low-right, a little drain doorway leads to level03, partly covered by a curled leaf which will unfold. Dry rim walkway connects entry, observation position and drain with no precision platforming.
Use warm terracotta outer shell and very light lavender indoor shadows with lots of paper-white glowing openings, a sheltering fairy-tale pot interior. Convey that camera rotation reveals real connectivity; no changing architecture, no projection-created bridge, no missing solid wall silently removed. No outgoing solved beam crossing clay.

A square corner pillar and masonry turn at x60% hide the following passage; do NOT draw ray through the opaque pillar. At the corner open gap x65–75%, a narrow glint/edge of the still-dark M2 can be seen in depth, making it discoverable. Use case: stylized-concept.
Input image 1 is a STRUCTURAL REFERENCE ONLY for the existing mirror prop: keep the brass frame, upright oval mirror, vertical shaft, fixed low gray base. Change its rendering to delicate hand-painted watercolor picture-book illustration with visible ivory paper, pigment granulation, fine sepia pencil, soft sage foliage and pale apricot/brass washes. Do not preserve the reference's hard cel-shading. Create a clean landscape prop-design sheet for the first three tutorial levels of 食光兽. Original fairy-tale objects, practical readable mechanisms. SIX spacious groups in a 3-column by 2-row arrangement, no scenic background, each with one concise Chinese title, large sketches and small state labels. This is a design sheet, no photorealism, no 3D-render shine.
Main title: '首三关｜交互与场景组件设计'.
GROUP 1 top-left: '旋镜｜固定底座・竖轴转向'. Show the SAME mirror at three YAW states: broad front, three-quarter, narrow right-side edge, all mirror faces remain exactly vertical, top and bottom vertically aligned, base stays fixed. Add a small TOP-VIEW diagram with a curved left-right arrow around the vertical axis, label '俯视'. Tiny lamplighter silhouette beside base shows scale, mirror center about 1.8 times character height; small reachable knob near base. Absolutely no pitch or rocking left/right in elevation.
GROUP 2 top-middle: '观察点｜同一空间・两个侧面'. A simple slender twig/bronze-ring viewing frame planted on safe mossy stone. Two tiny leaves decorate opposite sides. Show active observation A and B as small eye/camera-direction sketches around ONE stable room corner. Label '观察 A' and '观察 B'. Ring is a visual invitation to change viewpoint, not a portal or collectible key.
GROUP 3 top-right: '光鳞｜饥饿 → 吞光 → 安定'. Three close-ups of the SAME small patch of softly hairy warm-ivory living skin with translucent almond-shaped scale, states pale closed, slightly open drinking golden dust, softly glowing calm. No entire animal, no rock-texture, no mechanical button, no wounds.
GROUP 4 bottom-left: '卷叶出口｜闭合 → 舒展'. A real small cracked archway under root/terracotta rim: left sketch a curled broad leaf covers opening, right sketch same leaf curls aside after local plant revival. Opening and architecture remain identical. The passage becomes permanently accessible, shown by the small protagonist walking through in right sketch.
GROUP 5 bottom-middle: '平台组件｜石阶・陶片・渠沿'. Three side-elevation modular traversable shapes, each clear flat top, soft watercolor moss/terracotta/blue-gray brick. Add one tiny character beside a low step; short easy gap and shallow walk-out recovery slope. No sharp spikes, no dramatic pit, no ambiguous decorative walkable edges.
GROUP 6 bottom-right: '真实开口｜门缝・盆裂・转角'. Three simple wall cross-section vignettes: narrow gate opening, broken pot aperture, actual open L-corner. Opaque wall faces solid; thin golden line goes through open air/hole and around corner via an upright mirror, NEVER through wall. Tiny Chinese labels '门缝','盆裂','转角'.
Keep all marks in this same soft watercolor visual language, thin clear mechanism lines, sufficient white space. State diagrams must be accurate, legible and simple. Do not add lenses, dew focusing, colored-light locks or lever puzzles to these first-three-level components.

finalPropCleanupPrompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
The input is the EDIT TARGET: a watercolor first-three-level props sheet. Preserve all six groups, their watercolor drawings, title, colors, paper texture, prop silhouettes, state captions and layout.
This sheet should present ART APPEARANCE ONLY; exact geometry is provided in a separate engineering drawing. Clean up only these inaccurate technical overlays:
1. In group 1 TOP LEFT, remove the thin vertical dimension bracket and the text '约1.8倍角色高' at far left. Leave the tiny character and all THREE upright mirror variants intact. Do not change their relative illustration sizes.
2. In the same group 1, REMOVE the entire little diagram labelled '俯视' on the right side of that group: remove the word 俯视, the little base/mirror drawing, its two curved arrows, and its explanatory text below. Replace this little subarea with plain matching ivory paper. Keep the three main front/three-quarter/right-side mirror variants and their captions. Keep the group heading '旋镜｜固定底座・竖轴转向'.
3. In group 6 BOTTOM RIGHT, remove ALL golden light lines and ALL golden arrowheads from the THREE door/crack/corner vignettes. Keep the wall openings, upright mirrors, Chinese group title and labels 门缝/盆裂/转角. They are illustrative aperture examples, not optical ray diagrams.
Do not add any new text or new diagrams. Do not change the other groups or any scenic drawings. Full sheet uncropped.
